Title: GitHub - vbuterin/zkapi at feat/client-concession-local

URL Source: https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local

Markdown Content:
zkAPI lets you pay for AI and other APIs with ETH and make unlinkable requests. It keeps API usage separate from your on-chain deposit: the service can verify that you can pay without learning which deposit is yours.

Built by Open Anonymity in collaboration with the Ethereum Foundation, zkAPI uses zero-knowledge proofs to make this possible. Deposit ETH, pay only for what you use, and withdraw your remaining balance on-chain.

Live web app: [**chat.openanonymity.ai**](https://chat.openanonymity.ai/) — try zkAPI in OA Chat by choosing the Ethereum wallet option.

Documentation: [**zkapi.openanonymity.ai**](https://zkapi.openanonymity.ai/).

The protocol is experimental; see [the note-binding review](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/note-bound-commitments.md) and [the concession exit design](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/design/concession-exit.md), which lets a user withdraw without any cooperation from the operator.

Releases follow [semantic versioning](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/versioning.md) on major version 0: until 1.0.0, any interface may change in any release. See the [changelog](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/CHANGELOG.md).

## Privacy-enabled client development branch

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#privacy-enabled-client-development-branch)
This branch adds native Tor conversation isolation, canonical prompt rewriting, separate target-side history, bounded cover traffic and saved vault-protocol selection to the local client. Start with [the client README](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/zkapi-clientd/README.md) and [build instructions](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/zkapi-clientd/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

**Not a production release:** concession network manifests are undeployed and production proving keys are missing; legacy needs its matching historical wallet bundle. Neither protocol selection nor privacy features bypass these checks. Local wallets, binaries, proving assets and scratch outputs are excluded from Git.

## Local OpenAI-compatible API

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#local-openai-compatible-api)
Use [zkapi-clientd](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/zkapi-clientd/README.md) to configure an ETH wallet and serve inference to Open WebUI or another local OpenAI-compatible client. Its withdrawals can pay their network fee from the payout (`withdraw --fees payout`, through an ERC-4337 paymaster), so the payout address needs no ETH; the vault is unchanged.

## Build and test

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#build-and-test)

npm ci
npm test
npm run verify:assets
npm run verify:builds   # the placeholder profiles must refuse to build
cargo build --release --workspace
cargo test --release --workspace
cargo test --release --manifest-path protocol/rust/Cargo.toml --workspace
(cd protocol/contracts && forge test)

The protocol and required Solidity libraries are ordinary files in this repository. No submodule initialization, Cairo compiler or STARK prover is needed. See [source provenance](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/protocol/VENDORED.md).

## Browser SDK

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#browser-sdk)
`@openanonymity/zkapi-browser-sdk` owns native ETH funding, wallet persistence, proof generation, lease recovery, settlement and withdrawals. Mainnet and Sepolia have independent deployment pins, signing keys and wallet state. Applications configure the SDK before initializing a wallet; see [SDK integration](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/sdk/README.md) and [native billing](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/native-eth-billing.md). A withdrawal can pay its network fee from the payout (`fees: 'payout'`, through an ERC-4337 paymaster), so the payout address needs no ETH; the vault is unchanged.

The packaged WASM and proving keys support the current circuit `zkapi-v2-concession-v1` (vault revision 3), with the development setup until the multi-party ceremony has run. Until a revision-3 vault is deployed, the packaged network profiles are placeholders and `npm run build:browser` and `npm run build:mainnet` refuse them by design (`deployment_not_deployed`); `npm run verify:builds` checks exactly that. Notes of the earlier circuit `zkapi-v2-note-bound-v1` are served by the release line `release/v2-note-bound`. Ordinary SDK consumers do not need Rust. To rebuild WASM deliberately, use `scripts/build-browser-client.sh` and review the changed artifact hashes; `npm run verify:wasm` rebuilds it reproducibly and compares.

## Full local lifecycle acceptance

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#full-local-lifecycle-acceptance)
Run `npm run test:e2e:v2` to build and test circuit `zkapi-v2-concession-v1` end to end on a fresh local chain. It covers the honest flow and the Sepolia drill scenarios that run locally, and writes a gas report. The drill scenarios include withholding, bad successor anchors, a lying expiry check, forced and conceding escapes with raises and defeats, the bounded pause, a missed defeat with leaf retirement, and gasless withdrawals through a local bundler.

The contracts, proofs, server, indexer, challenger, signer sidecar, browser SDK and clientd companion are real. The provider, OA org and price feed are mocked. See the [acceptance process and coverage limits](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/v2-acceptance.md). `node scripts/check-withdrawal-golden.mjs` submits the Rust, JS and Go withdrawal encoders' calldata to an Anvil vault.

## Operator services

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#operator-services)
*   `zkapi serverd`: native ETH lease authorization, settlement and Schnorr signing.
*   `zkapi-indexerd` / `zkapi indexer`: vault event indexing and Merkle paths from a view verified against the vault.
*   `zkapi db init`: create the server database with its append-only request evidence and bind it to the deployment manifest, before any daemon starts.
*   `zkapi-challenged`: durable escape monitoring; defeats escapes from spent states, raises under-conceded escapes, and retires a closed note's leaf after a missed defeat; private status endpoints.
*   `zkapi signing-keys`: derive deployment public keys from operator seeds (the published development keys are rejected).
*   `zkapi settlement reopen`: with the API server stopped, verify, repair and reopen a lease cancelled for a corrupt binding.
*   `zkapi setup --output-dir NEW_DIRECTORY`: generate a fresh single-party development setup, which release builds refuse.

Native server startup requires a pinned oracle RPC/feed, a lease issuer, the deployment manifest, and both `ZKAPI_STATE_SEED` and `ZKAPI_CLEAR_SEED`; there are no default seeds. The server refuses to start unless their keys equal the vault's immutable keys and the vault, adapter and Poseidon library match the manifest. Use [deployment instructions](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/deployment.md), [Docker operation](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docker/aws/README.md), [challenge service operation](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/challenge-service.md) and the [concession-vault migration runbook](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/migration-concession-vault.md). The browser sends prompts directly to the inference provider; the server handles authorization and settlement.

The keys in `protocol/setup/v2-concession` (the ceremony's, once G-SETUP has run) must match the vault's immutable verifier and the client's pinned proof artifacts; `protocol/setup/v2-concession-dev` holds the development keys for tests, the drill vault and vaults deliberately deployed on a single-party setup ([Single-party setup](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/docs/deployment.md#single-party-setup)). The `setup` command generates new development keys; it is not part of connecting a client to the configured vault.

## Protocol details

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#protocol-details)
The active protocol uses Groth16 over BN254, Poseidon, note-bound Baby-JubJub commitments and Schnorr signatures, a nullifier chain whose successor anchors are derived from the spent nullifier, and a 32-level append-only Merkle tree. The ledger uses integer gwei. An escape concedes at most the request budget of the state it leaves and needs no operator cooperation. Production keys need the multi-party setup described in [the ceremony setup](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/blob/feat/client-concession-local/protocol/setup/v2-concession/README.md); the committed keys are a single-party development setup.

## Source layout

[](https://github.com/vbuterin/zkapi/tree/feat/client-concession-local#source-layout)
| Directory | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `zkapi-clientd/` | Local ETH-funded OpenAI-compatible client and installer |
| `sdk/` | Browser native ETH wallet, public artifacts and SDK tests |
| `protocol/rust/` | Shared v2 types, BN254 helpers, circuits and Rust/WASM wallets |
| `protocol/contracts/` | Native ETH vault, Groth16 verifier and contract tests |
| `protocol/setup/v2-concession/`, `v2-concession-dev/` | Ceremony and development setups of the current circuit |
| `protocol/setup/v2/` | Setup of the legacy circuit, for `release/v2-note-bound` |
| `crates/` | Operator CLI, server, indexer, challenger and the clientd wallet companion |
| `demo/contracts/` | Native ETH verifier/vault deployment script |
| `docker/aws/` | API/indexer/challenger image configuration and restricted signer |
